ai.instructions:
- Users usually refer to services by name. Always call get-services first to resolve a service name to its service ID before calling tools that take a serviceId.
- Prefer targeted purges (purge-url or purge-surrogate-keys) over purge-all. Only use purge-all when the user explicitly asks to purge everything on a service.
- Prefer soft purges unless the user asks for a hard purge or needs content gone immediately (e.g. removing sensitive content).
- When showing TLS certificates, call out any certificate expiring within 30 days.
- AI Runtime Control tools return an entitlement error on accounts without the product; relay that message rather than retrying.
- Never display API tokens, access tokens, or secret values in responses.
- Format bandwidth in human-readable units (MB, GB) and timestamps as readable dates.

expected.meetsCriteria: Lists both services with their types

evals.input: @fastly how's the cache hit ratio on www.example.com?

expected.meetsCriteria: Reports the cache hit ratio of about 93%

evals.input: @fastly are we under a DDoS attack right now?

expected.meetsCriteria: Says there is an ongoing attack and mentions when it started

evals.input: @fastly do any of my TLS certs expire soon?

expected.meetsCriteria: Warns that the www.example.com certificate expires in 11 days

evals.input: @fastly is bot management enabled on www.example.com?

expected.meetsCriteria: Says Bot Management is enabled and summarizes detected bot traffic
Confirms the whole cache was purged

evals.input: @fastly are any alerts firing right now?

expected.meetsCriteria: Says the High origin errors alert is currently firing

evals.input: @fastly what changed on my account in the last day?

expected.meetsCriteria: Summarizes the version activation and token creation events

evals.input: @fastly how many AI tokens did we use this week?

expected.meetsCriteria: Summarizes input and output token usage
